title: mechanical cam archive geometry 001
instruction:
You are Laila Fitzgerald, the mechanical engineer at Pinehollow Health Network, preparing a replacement-part drawing for a small working print museum that is taking in a 1961 Brennerhoff & Sohn platen press from Cormac Schuyler. The press's impression cam is cracked, and the museum will accept the machine only if the replacement can be documented and filed beside the surviving maker's drawings. Heronbank Terminals is cutting the part for us, so the sheet needs to give a machinist usable dimensions while remaining recognisably consistent with the period archive. Use the two archive drawing sheets in `archive_sheet_01.pdf` and `archive_sheet_02.pdf`, the measured cam and shaft record in `cam_measurements.xlsx`, the museum's acceptance note in `museum_acceptance_note.docx`, and the supplied drawing-sheet reference in `archive_convention_reference.pdf` when preparing the work. Create exactly one file named `replacement_impression_cam_drawing.xlsx` and write it at the top level of the working directory. It will be printed on A3 paper in landscape orientation, placed in a sleeve, and shelved next to the original sheets; keep the drawing readable at that physical size and make the views, dimensions, notes, title information, and first-angle convention agree with the supplied material. The drawing must be a reusable working sheet rather than a completed inspection record: include the part definition and machining information, but leave the measured-result and approval/signature entries empty. The registrar has asked for a clearly bounded place where a later measured value or deviation can be written even when it is longer than the ordinary value, without pushing the surrounding drawing out of alignment, and for short pickup guidance so the next engineer knows what the blank fields mean without the guidance taking over the sheet. Do not add a modern logo, colour branding, extra views, unsupported tolerances, or recommendations about whether the museum should accept the press. Preserve the supplied archive's units, line hierarchy, lettering character, pre-GD&T limit style, and first-angle reading. Keep the workbook functional and easy to inspect, with the drawing sheet as the only printable sheet.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/archive_sheet_01.pdf` — First surviving Brennerhoff & Sohn archive drawing showing the period sheet convention, view arrangement, lettering, line hierarchy, title-block language, and first-angle projection.
- `references/archive_sheet_02.pdf` — Second surviving archive drawing used to corroborate the historical dimensioning, limit notation, notes-block treatment, and drawing-sheet proportions.
- `references/cam_measurements.xlsx` — Complete and internally consistent measurement record for the cracked cam, mating shaft, keyway, and replacement-part envelope.
- `references/museum_acceptance_note.docx` — Museum filing and acceptance requirements, including the identification wording and the information that must remain blank until inspection.
- `references/archive_convention_reference.pdf` — Reference extract defining the reproducible sheet geometry, projection symbol treatment, line-weight hierarchy, and period lettering and limit conventions to be used when comparing the finished workbook.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `replacement_impression_cam_drawing.xlsx` — A single-sheet, printable replacement impression-cam detail drawing laid out as an A3 landscape archive-style drawing sheet. (The workbook must contain exactly one worksheet and exactly one printable drawing sheet.; The sheet must print as one A3 landscape page, fitted to one page wide and one page tall.; The drawing geometry, dimensions, notes, title information, and first-angle convention must be derived from the supplied references.; Measured-result and approval/signature fields must remain completely empty.; The sheet must include a bounded expandable deviation or out-of-range-value area and concise pickup guidance.; Do not add logos, colour branding, unsupported tolerances, or recommendations.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

materials.text:
Museum intake and drawing filing note
Pinehollow Health Network is preparing a replacement impression cam for the 1961 Brennerhoff & Sohn platen press, model P-17, received from Cormac Schuyler. File the drawing beside the surviving maker sheets.
Use drawing number 61-CAM-017, initial revision A. The prepared-by field should identify Laila Fitzgerald, Mechanical Engineer. Material is to remain the source wording: steel. Units are millimetres.
The sheet is a working drawing. Leave inspection result, inspection date, approval/signature, and any deviation entry blank until the machined part is inspected.

sheets.name: CAM DETAIL
rows:
1  ALL DIMENSIONS IN MILLIMETRES UNLESS OTHERWISE SHOWN.
2  LIMITS ARE SHOWN AS PAIRED VALUES; NO GENERAL TOLERANCE APPLIES.
3  DATUM A IS THE SHAFT AXIS; KEYWAY CENTRELINE IS 0° FROM DATUM A.
4  MATERIAL: STEEL. BREAK SHARP EDGES 0.50 (0.30 / 0.70).
5  PROFILE: BASE R34.00, NOSE R41.00, RISE 7.00; START 35° (34.5 / 35.5), END 145° (144.5 / 145.5).
6  BORE Ø25.00 (24.98 / 25.00); MATING SHAFT Ø24.95 (24.93 / 24.95).
7  KEYWAY 8.00 (7.98 / 8.02) WIDE × 3.30 (3.25 / 3.35) DEEP × 22.00 (21.90 / 22.10) LONG.

PREPARED BY
Laila Fitzgerald, Mechanical Engineer
ARCHIVE COMPATIBLE LIMIT STYLE — NO GENERAL TOLERANCE

spec.professional_context: This is a period-compatible mechanical drawing for a one-off replacement part being machined and then filed as museum documentation. The downstream users are a machinist, a museum registrar, and a later engineer who must be able to read the sheet without reconstructing its conventions.
difficulty_sources: Reproduce a period drawing convention from two supplied archive sheets.
Translate a complete measurement record into a coherent, machinable replacement-part drawing.
Preserve first-angle layout, line hierarchy, note placement, and pre-GD&T limits.
Design a bounded out-of-range-value area and concise pickup guidance without compromising the drawing geometry.
Produce an editable, one-page A3 landscape workbook that renders correctly offline.

print.margins: archive-compatible narrow margins with visible border

required_geometry: One primary cam profile view in the upper-left region.
One mating shaft-axis view in the upper-right region.
One keyway or mating-feature detail view in the lower-right region.
A bounded notes block in the lower-left region.
A first-angle projection symbol in the upper-right corner region.
A distinct bounded deviation area with wrapped editable text capacity, kept empty.
A compact bounded pickup-guidance area, separate from the main views.
A six-row title block spanning the bottom of the sheet.

source_derivation.archive_sheet_01.pdf: Use for first-angle arrangement, border and title-block character, line hierarchy, note placement, and lettering.
source_derivation.archive_sheet_02.pdf: Use to corroborate period limit notation, dimension presentation, and view/detail conventions.
source_derivation.cam_measurements.xlsx: Use as the sole source for cam, bore, shaft, keyway, envelope, angular, and mating dimensions.
source_derivation.museum_acceptance_note.docx: Use for filing identity, drawing-number wording, blank inspection fields, and required museum documentation language.
source_derivation.archive_convention_reference.pdf: Use for exact reproducible sheet geometry, projection-symbol placement, and the controlled visual convention.

deterministic_rules: Every required dimension in the measurement record must appear in the appropriate view or notes.
Use the measurement-record units and precision.
Use the archive's pre-GD&T limit style and do not invent general tolerances.
Keep notes inside the bounded notes block.
Keep the deviation area and inspection fields empty.
Keep guidance concise and inside its bounded region.
Do not introduce logos, unsupported specifications, recommendations, or additional views.
behaviour_specification.out_of_range affordance: The deviation area must be a separate bordered merged/wrapped region with enough horizontal and vertical capacity for a longer handwritten or typed measurement and explanatory note. It must not alter adjacent view coordinates or title-block boundaries.
behaviour_specification.pickup_guidance: Include short plain-language guidance explaining that nominal dimensions and limits are design information, that measured results are entered only after inspection, and that an out-of-range measurement belongs in the deviation area.

authoring_plan.gold_construction: Build a clean XLSX with editable cells, borders, text, and drawing lines using openpyxl. Populate only design dimensions and source-supported notes; leave all designated blank fields truly empty. Set page setup, print area, margins, scaling, and sheet visibility explicitly. Render offline to verify one A3 landscape page and compare the render with both archive PDFs. The gold passes when all source dimensions and identifiers are present, the structural regions match the schema, the blank fields contain no values or formulas, and the standalone rendered sheet is readable and period-compatible.

deliverables.description: A single-sheet, printable replacement impression-cam detail drawing laid out as an A3 landscape archive-style drawing sheet.
constraints: The workbook must contain exactly one worksheet and exactly one printable drawing sheet.
The sheet must print as one A3 landscape page, fitted to one page wide and one page tall.
The drawing geometry, dimensions, notes, title information, and first-angle convention must be derived from the supplied references.
Measured-result and approval/signature fields must remain completely empty.
The sheet must include a bounded expandable deviation or out-of-range-value area and concise pickup guidance.
Do not add logos, colour branding, unsupported tolerances, or recommendations.
